subject: Post-call: FinServe TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: James Sutherland <j.sutherland@finserve.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinServe TCO recap & next steps

Hi James —

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Wanted to summarize the call and surface the cost levers we discussed so your procurement and engineering teams can evaluate TCO quickly.

Key pain / goals (as we heard):
- High per-request cost on current LLM provider when processing large document sets (month-end run spikes).
- Strict budget for POC: ~$50k run-rate target for sustained usage.
- Need predictable latency for customer-facing search (95th percentile < 250ms).
- Data residency and audit logs are required for compliance.

Redwood TCO summary (high level):
- Token economics: based on the sample workload you shared (avg 320 tokens/request, 1.2M requests/month), estimated baseline hosted cost with our standard model = ~$28k/month.
- Batching & caching opportunity: enabling 1) request-level batching and 2) prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts reduces tokens served and GPU overhead — we estimate a 20–35% cost reduction depending on cache hit rate.
- Quantization + model profile: moving to an optimized quantized variant for production inference reduces per-token compute by ~30% with negligible quality change on your prompts (we validated on your sample).
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoff: at your 1.2M rps/month, Dedicated reserved capacity with a 12-month commit would likely shave another ~15–25% off unit cost vs hosted API, while giving you SLA and traffic isolation.

Deliverables attached:
- FinServe_TCO_Model.xlsx — editable cost model with assumptions (token counts, hit rates, batch sizes).
- redwood_cost_playbook.pdf — recommended configuration (batching thresholds, cache policies, quantization profile).
- redwood-sla.pdf — example SLA for Dedicated.

Open questions / assumptions to validate:
1) Is the 1.2M requests/month number representative of steady-state or peak (month-end)?
2) Typical prompt distribution: we used avg 320 tokens with 15% variance; can you confirm sample sizes for short/long prompts?
3) Acceptable latency SLO for canary traffic — do you want us to target 95p < 250ms or < 200ms?

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael to run a quick inference cost sim on your exact sample corpus (ETA: Monday).
- We’ll provision a short-lived Dedicated trial if you want to validate performance at scale (requires a quick procurement signature).
- Quick follow-up call early next week to walk through the Excel model and finalize assumptions.

If this matches your view, I’ll loop in procurement and schedule the follow-up.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: FinServe_TCO_Model.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_cost_playbook.pdf (guide), redwood-sla.pdf (pdf)

From: James Sutherland <j.sutherland@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinServe Procurement <procurement@finserve.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinServe TCO recap & next steps

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap and the model. A couple quick clarifications before we share with procurement: 
- The 1.2M requests/month is steady-state expected after Q1; month-end spikes can push that to ~1.8M for a 72-hour window.
- Prompt mix: about 70% short (<=120 tokens), 20% medium (121–450), 10% long (>450).
- Latency: we should target 95p < 200ms for the search use case; fallback to 250ms for lower-priority workloads is acceptable.

Procurement question: for the Dedicated trial, what’s the minimum commit and is there a way to do a short-term eval with reduced financial commitment? They prefer a 3-month pilot cap.

Happy to hop on the follow-up call. Are Rafael and Naomi available Tuesday morning PST?

—James
James Sutherland
Head of Product — Search
FinServe Inc.
j.sutherland@finserve.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinServe TCO recap & next steps

Thanks James — that mix is super helpful and actually improves the cost estimate (higher short-prompt ratio reduces avg tokens).

Responding to procurement — short answers: 
- Minimum commit: for Dedicated we typically recommend a 6–12 month reserved commitment to realize the unit-cost savings. However, we offer a limited 3-month pilot program (lower commit, higher unit price) specifically for evaluation — that sounds like a good fit for FinServe to validate latency and end-to-end integration.
- Pilot includes: access to a Dedicated pool sized for your peak testing window, observability dashboard, and a 1:1 onboarding session with Naomi (SRE lead) + Rafael for performance tuning.

Rafael: can you run the cost sim against James' updated prompt mix and the 1.8M peak window? Naomi: can you block 60 mins Tuesday 9am PST for the technical canary plan?

James — I’ll share a revised FinServe_TCO_Model.xlsx with the updated assumptions by EOD today and book the Tuesday slot once Rafael/Naomi confirm.

Best,
Marissa
